raw_finding.practical_consequence: A fresh planner would have to invent a local Codex action-dispatch hook or incorrectly treat advisory skill compliance as enforced interception, so it cannot produce grounded READY records for universal action observation, pre-dispatch sequence activation, or the local real-boundary acceptance proof.
evidence: Candidate research_markdown CUR-002 states that recognition is advisory before governed-path entry and that no accessible Codex-host source proves arbitrary pre-dispatch interception.
Candidate research_markdown CUR-007 states that file edits, browser actions, generic MCP/tool calls, and subagent actions have no work-memory producers.

E-SKILL-DEPLOYED says the deployed skill is advisory and explicitly does not expose Codex host internals; E-CODEX-CLI and E-EXECUTOR expose only the remote workflow outer invocation boundary, not local ordered action dispatch.
E-REQ requires every in-scope action class to have a named authoritative producer and requires exact compatible-sequence selection before dispatch.
raw_finding.evidence_limitation: The frozen roots contain no local Codex host dispatch/instrumentation boundary, and the candidate names neither a custodian nor an authorized acquisition route for that missing contract.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: Actions outside guarded direct argv cannot currently become authoritative learning evidence, so the complete system needs explicit producer coverage for each supported dispatch surface and a visible unsupported result for the rest.
evidence: E-CHECKEXEC and E-WORKMEM ground the current argv producer boundary.
E-EXECUTOR, E-CLI-BASE, and E-CODEX-CLI ground the aggregate-only remote boundary.
E-REQ defines the required action-class coverage matrix.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A matching registered sequence can still be bypassed when the model improvises before entering the governed path, so planning must place applicability and enforcement before effect dispatch while preserving approval gates.
evidence: E-SKILL-REPO and E-SKILL-DEPLOYED establish advisory entry behavior.
E-GUARD establishes fail-closed enforcement only after activation.
E-OBSERVER establishes post-close matching rather than pre-dispatch interception.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: An eligible success can create a discovery, but qualification, promotion, registered verification, and later reuse still require explicit driving, so the success-learning loop is not closed end to end.
evidence: E-OBSERVER and E-BOOTSTRAP establish automatic eligible discovery creation.
E-LIFECYCLE and E-E2E establish explicitly driven qualification, promotion, registered verification, and later linking.
E-REQ defines the required lifecycle-spanning proof.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A model statement that its own action caused a failure cannot currently authorize or construct a reusable correction, so planning must join the signal to authoritative action, failure, blocker, replacement, and same-path successor evidence.
evidence: E-BLOCKER and E-WORKMEM ground blocker, correction, and successor-verification records.
E-OBSERVER explicitly lacks the model-diagnosis causal join.
E-REQ defines the evidence-backed correction and non-repetition outcomes.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A defective registered sequence lacks an immutable replacement identity and atomic selector cutover, so planning must preserve the old version as auditable and non-selectable while requalifying and verifying its replacement.
evidence: E-LIFECYCLE and E-PROMOTE ground the current lifecycle and registration authority.
E-RECON and E-WORKMEM ground existing reconciliation and bundle transitions but explicitly lack immutable registered-version replacement semantics.
E-REQ defines quarantine, requalification, registered verification, and atomic cutover.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The system cannot currently distinguish silver from gold or show whether learning reduces repeated mistakes, so planning must define machine-readable transitions and denominator-based capture, reuse, correction, false-match, hold, and recurrence metrics.
evidence: E-REGISTRY, E-WORKMEM, and E-OBSERVER establish that current contracts contain neither silver/gold states nor the required effectiveness metrics.
E-REQ defines the lifecycle and measurement acceptance boundaries.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: Separate sequence and workflow stores can resume independently without a declared cross-runtime merge and current-version owner, so planning must assign canonical ownership and explicit idempotent resume, event-union, conflict, and cutover rules.
evidence: E-WORKMEM, E-RECON, and E-PROMOTE ground the sequence-side ledger and lifecycle state.
E-WORKFLOW-STATE grounds a separate atomic workflow/phase store with no sequence merge contract.
E-REQ defines interruption, branch-safety, and immutable feedback requirements.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A planner cannot safely preserve or replace the current lifecycle because the candidate does not state exactly how promotion, registered verification, reuse, supersession, and correction feedback currently affect later selection and observer decisions.
evidence: CUR-005 explicitly requires exact current promotion, registered-verification, reuse, supersession, and correction-feedback semantics.

candidate-round-1.json requirement_statuses[CUR-005] reports only durable_lifecycle, in-place repair, and absence of immutable cutover; research_markdown CUR-005 repeats that summary without decomposing all five required lifecycle behaviors.
E-LIFECYCLE, E-RECON, E-OBSERVER, E-PROMOTE, and E-WORKMEM are available frozen-root evidence capable of grounding the omitted current semantics.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The implementation planner must provide authoritative safe producers for every in-scope action class; otherwise non-argv behavior will remain invisible to sequence learning.
evidence: E-REQ defines universal authoritative action observation and visible handling of unsupported classes.
E-WORKMEM and E-CHECKEXEC establish that the current canonical action record is limited to guarded argv execution.
E-EXECUTOR, E-CLI-BASE, E-CODEX-CLI, and E-WORKFLOW-STATE establish aggregate remote execution records without canonical per-action events.
candidate-round-1.json CUR-001, CUR-007, and FUT-001 provide the grounded current boundary and future producer/event contract.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner must place exact sequence applicability and governed activation before effect dispatch while preserving approval separation; otherwise a model can improvise before the existing guard becomes relevant.
evidence: E-REQ defines pre-dispatch matching, fail-visible rejection, and separate observer and approval authorities.
E-SKILL-REPO, E-SKILL-DEPLOYED, E-WORKMEM, and E-GUARD establish that current recognition is advisory before governed-path entry.
candidate-round-1.json CUR-002, FUT-002, and FUT-012 reconcile mandatory governed routing with the prohibition on observer-owned execution or approval.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner must connect proven unrecorded success through complete discovery, qualification, promotion, registered verification, and later pre-dispatch reuse; today only eligible discovery capture is automatic.
evidence: E-REQ defines the complete success-learning lifecycle and its real-boundary acceptance proof.
E-OBSERVER and E-BOOTSTRAP establish eligible checked-exec discovery creation.
E-LIFECYCLE, E-PROMOTE, and E-E2E establish that qualification, promotion, and registered verification are explicitly driven.
candidate-round-1.json CUR-003, FUT-003, FUT-007, and FUT-014 provide the required candidate completeness and terminal lifecycle outcomes.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner must join a model's self-identified mistake to authoritative action, failure, blocker, replacement, and same-path successor evidence; otherwise self-diagnosis cannot safely change a reusable sequence.
evidence: E-REQ distinguishes a high-value self-diagnosis signal from evidence-backed causal authority.
E-BLOCKER and E-WORKMEM establish existing blocker, correction, bundle-transition, and successor-verification evidence.
E-OBSERVER and E-EXECUTOR establish the absence of a current self-diagnosis-to-exact-action repair join.
candidate-round-1.json CUR-004, FUT-004, FUT-005, and FUT-014 define the causal proof and non-repetition outcome.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner must replace defective registered content through quarantine, immutable versioning, requalification, registered verification, and atomic selector cutover so the known-wrong step cannot be selected again.
evidence: E-REQ defines versioned repair, retained auditability, non-selectability of the old version, and gated eligibility of the replacement.
E-WORKMEM and E-LIFECYCLE establish the current in-place bundle-transition correction model.
E-PROMOTE and E-RECON establish promotion and reconciliation without immutable registered replacement versions.
candidate-round-1.json FUT-005, FUT-006, and FUT-013 provide the corrected-path, cutover, provenance, and version-bound feedback outcomes.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner must turn silver, gold, their lifecycle transitions, and learning effectiveness into machine-readable states and denominator-backed metrics; otherwise growth and recurrence reduction cannot be distinguished from raw event volume.
evidence: E-REQ defines silver and gold lifecycle obligations and the complete effectiveness metric set.
E-REGISTRY, E-WORKMEM, and E-OBSERVER establish that current contracts have neither canonical silver/gold states nor the required learning-effectiveness measures.

candidate-round-1.json FUT-007 and FUT-008 define the state meanings, transition categories, eligible-opportunity denominators, reuse outcomes, false matches, evidence holds, and wrong-step recurrence measures.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: The planner must assign canonical ownership and deterministic resume, merge, conflict, identity, and current-version rules across local, remote, concurrent, and branch-separated runs; otherwise corrections or sequence versions can be duplicated, lost, or selected stale.
evidence: E-REQ defines durable resumable multi-run and branch-safe learning state plus deduplication and immutable feedback.
E-WORKMEM and E-RECON establish local ledger merge and reconciliation boundaries.
E-WORKFLOW-STATE establishes a separate per-run remote state store without sequence-version synchronization.
candidate-round-1.json FUT-009, FUT-010, and FUT-013 provide the identity, suppression, ownership, resume, branch-conflict, and versioned-consumption outcomes.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A planner would treat successful run close as a reliably automatic learning trigger, although capture can be disabled, skipped when context is absent, or fail after the run is already committed; those cases materially change whether a successful path enters discovery.
evidence: Required behavior: requirements.json:3-16 requires the exact current trigger and observation boundary, while requirements.json:51-64 requires every automatic, opt-in, and manual success-learning transition.

Demonstrated omitted behavior: scripts/work_memory.py:1998-2025 commits run_closed first, invokes the observer only for enabled mode or auto mode with operation context and MK_SEQUENCE_OBSERVER_DISABLED != 1, catches every observer exception, and surfaces DISABLED or OBSERVER_FAILED without rolling back the terminal run.

Candidate omission: candidate-round-1.json requirement_statuses for CUR-001 and CUR-003 and research_markdown sections CUR-001/CUR-003 describe post-close automatic capture but do not state the mode, environment, context prerequisites, committed-before-observation ordering, or failure degradation.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: Planning from the candidate would recreate measurement capabilities that already exist and would not clearly distinguish reusable current correction/outcome metrics from the genuinely missing sequence-learning denominators and lifecycle metrics.
evidence: Required behavior: requirements.json:123-135 asks which outcome metrics currently exist, and requirements.json:333-344 defines the additional future learning-loop metrics.

Demonstrated current behavior: scripts/work_memory.py:2050-2082 computes closed-run, pass, first-pass-success, corrections-per-run, repeated-blocker, same-path-verification, and duration metrics with explicit denominators; scripts/work_memory.py:2096-2148 computes trend and before/after correction-bundle change effects.

Candidate contradiction: candidate-round-1.json records CUR-006 research_value.learning_effectiveness_metrics as false, even though its prose only supports the narrower conclusion that silver/gold lifecycle, eligible-observation, reuse, false-match, evidence-hold, and known-wrong-step-recurrence metrics are absent.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A planner cannot assign a concrete producer and enforcement boundary for each missing action class because file edits, browser actions, generic MCP/tool calls, subagent actions, and reasoning self-reports are collapsed into one unsupported statement instead of being traced individually.
evidence: Required behavior: requirements.json:146-160 requires each named action class to be mapped to its producer, durable record, observer consumer, enforcement point, or confirmed absence.

Demonstrated implemented side: scripts/sequence_checked_exec.py:38-108 is the only repository producer joining guard, execution_claimed, shell-false argv dispatch, and execution_returned; scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-196 reconstructs candidates only from operation context plus those claim/return pairs.
Demonstrated remote side: mcp-agents-workflow/src/workflow_orch/cli/base.py:50-78 exposes aggregate invocation response fields rather than canonical ordered action events.

Candidate insufficiency: candidate-round-1.json CUR-007 reports one argv row, one aggregate remote row, and a single 'other_action_classes' absence. Its evidence index contains no per-class producer/consumer trace or bounded authoritative-root absence result for file-edit, browser, MCP/tool, subagent, and reasoning classes.
raw_finding.evidence_limitation: The accessible roots are sufficient to perform and index the missing per-class trace; the current candidate has not done so.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: Without new authoritative producers, successful or failed non-argv model actions cannot enter the learning loop and unsupported surfaces cannot fail visibly.
evidence: requirements.json:170-183 requires a named producer, safe event, stable identity, outcome link, and observer consumer for every in-scope action class.

scripts/sequence_checked_exec.py:38-108 and scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-196 establish the reusable argv producer/consumer pattern; mcp-agents-workflow/src/workflow_orch/cli/base.py:50-78 establishes the current aggregate-only remote boundary.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A matching registered sequence is not guaranteed to intercept effect dispatch, so the model can still improvise before selection and guard enforcement begin.
evidence: requirements.json:194-206 requires a matching gold sequence to be selected before dispatch.

scripts/work_memory.py:1314-1383 selects by operation kind, optional explicit sequence ID, or verified blocker fingerprint and returns ambiguity instead of intercepting dispatch; scripts/sequence_guard.py:568-729 enforces only after selection and activation.

scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-196 and 534-584 build and compare full identities only after a completed run, so the planner must define a distinct pre-dispatch applicability contract compatible with the proven post-run identity.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A proven unrecorded success can become a discovery, but it does not autonomously traverse qualification, promotion, registered verification, and later pre-dispatch reuse.
evidence: requirements.json:217-229 and 471-484 require canonical success capture and a lifecycle-spanning reuse proof.
scripts/sequence_observer.py:1104-1127 can propose/bootstrap a discovery after close; scripts/discovery_promotion_lifecycle.py:380-415 exposes an explicitly driven lifecycle controller.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A model saying that its own action caused a failure cannot currently produce an authoritative repair candidate or prevent that step from recurring without a separate governed action/failure/correction join.
evidence: requirements.json:240-275 requires self-diagnosis to remain a signal while grounded action, failure, blocker, replacement, and successor evidence supply causal authority.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: Correcting a registered sequence does not create a quarantined, independently requalified replacement version with an atomic selector cutover, so old and corrected eligibility cannot be managed as immutable versions.
evidence: requirements.json:286-299 requires versioned replacement, auditability, quarantine, requalification, registered verification, and atomic cutover.

scripts/discovery_promotion_lifecycle.py exposes registered correction and successor verification, while scripts/sequence_promote.py:222-384 materializes discovery-to-registration without a registered replacement-version identity.
scripts/work_memory.py:2133-2147 compares old and new bundle hashes but does not define selector-visible immutable sequence versions.
